cpu.name: Cortex-M0+ CPU
cpu.note: 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+; up to 80 MHz, 32 MHz in these builds

nvic.name: Interrupts
nvic.note: interrupts; none are enabled in these builds

dma.name: DMA
dma.note: moves data without the CPU; these builds do not use it

clk.name: Clocks and power
clk.note: the 32 MHz oscillator and the supply

uart0.name: UART0
uart0.note: serial port; its pins go to the probe

blink.title: Blink an LED
blink.card_line: No wiring: LED1 is on the board. The blink demo built into the Lab page drives the red LED2 instead.
blink.wiring: Nothing to wire. LED1 is on the board.

rows.step: Drives the pin high, then low

hobby-button-knob-dim.title: Button, knob and dimmer
hobby-button-knob-dim.card_line: Turn a knob and an LED dims.
hobby-button-knob-dim.wiring: Knob wiper to J1 pin 2 (PA25), its ends to J1 pin 1 (3V3) and J2 pin 20 (GND). LED anode through 330 Ω to J4 pin 40 (PB4), cathode to GND. S2 is on the board; optional: your own button on J2 pin 15 (PB8), other side to GND.

rows.step: Turns it into a pulse width

rows.by: PA10, J4 pin 34, through the probe

hobby-led-sequences.title: Traffic light, reaction game, tune
hobby-led-sequences.card_line: Three lamps, two buttons and a tune.
hobby-led-sequences.wiring: Red LED to J2 pin 11 (PB16), yellow to J2 pin 18 (PB17), green to J2 pin 19 (PB12), each through 330 Ω, cathodes to GND. Second button from J2 pin 15 (PB8) to GND. Passive buzzer to J2 pin 14 (PB7). S2 is on the board.

rows.by: PA10, J4 pin 34, through the probe

hobby-parking-sensor.title: Parking sensor
hobby-parking-sensor.card_line: A buzzer beeps faster as you get close.
hobby-parking-sensor.wiring: Sensor TRIG to J4 pin 35 (PB13), ECHO to J4 pin 36 (PB20), VCC to J1 pin 1 (3V3), GND to J2 pin 20 (GND). Buzzer to J2 pin 14 (PB7), its other leg to GND.

rows.step: Sends a ping ten times a second

rows.by: GPIOB PB20, high until it returns
TIMG8 CC1, 2 kHz, PB7 J2 pin 14
PA10, J4 pin 34, through the probe

hobby-weather-station.title: Room weather station
hobby-weather-station.card_line: Temperature and humidity on a small screen.
hobby-weather-station.wiring: DHT11 DATA to J1 pin 7 (PB9). OLED SCL to J1 pin 9 (PB2), SDA to J1 pin 10 (PB3). Both to 3V3 and GND. A bare DHT11 needs 4.7 to 10 kΩ from DATA to 3V3; the 3-pin module has it.

rows.by: GPIOB PB9, one wire, every 2 s
GPIOB PB2, PB3 as I2C by hand

rows.step: Times the sensor pulses and the I2C clock

rows.by: PA10, J4 pin 34, through the probe

near.i2c1: Its pins PB2 and PB3 are used as plain GPIO here: this build does the I2C itself to stay small.

hobby-servo-pantilt.title: Servo on a knob, then pan and tilt
hobby-servo-pantilt.card_line: A knob turns the servo; two make pan and tilt.
hobby-servo-pantilt.wiring: Pots to J1 pin 2 (PA25) and J1 pin 6 (PB24), their ends to J1 pin 1 (3V3) and J2 pin 20 (GND). Servo signals to J4 pin 40 (PB4) and J4 pin 39 (PB1); servo power from J3 pin 21 (5V), grounds joined to J3 pin 22 (GND). Wire servo 1 first; the program drives both.

rows.step: Turns each into a pulse, 1 to 2 ms

rows.by: PA10, J4 pin 34, through the probe

hobby-pir-alarm.title: Motion alarm with a counter
hobby-pir-alarm.card_line: Counts each movement and sounds a buzzer.
hobby-pir-alarm.wiring: PIR OUT to J2 pin 12 (PB0), PIR power from J3 pin 21 (5V). Display CLK to J4 pin 40 (PB4), DIO to J4 pin 39 (PB1), VCC to J1 pin 1 (3V3). Buzzer to J2 pin 14 (PB7). Grounds to J2 pin 20 (GND). The display shows dashes for the first 30 s while the PIR warms up.

rows.by: GPIOB PB4, PB1, two wires by hand
PA10, J4 pin 34, through the probe
